title: Exact linear functors preserve the signed Koszul completion model
statement:
Let $(\mathcal C,R)$ and $(\mathcal D,S)$ be small ringed sites with commutative structure sheaves $R,S$, and let a commutative ring $A$ act on $R,S$ by global sections. Let $F:\operatorname{Mod}(R)\to\operatorname{Mod}(S)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] be additive [def-weil-pbc-additive-functor], exact and $A$-linear: $F(a f)=aF(f)$ for every $a\in A$ and module map $f$. Suppose its canonical countable-product comparison [def-weil-category-product] $F(\prod_m M_m)\to\prod_m F(M_m)$, characterized by the projections, is invertible. Assume countable products are exact in both module categories. Fix $r\ge0$ and $a_1,\ldots,a_r\in A$. For $m\ge1$ set $Q_m(R)=\bigotimes_{i=1}^r[R\xrightarrow{a_i^m}R]$ in degrees $[-r,0]$, with transitions multiplication by $a_i$ in degree $-1$ and identity in degree $0$ in each factor; define $Q_m(S)$ similarly. Use the total tensor convention [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. For a complex $C$, set $B_R(C)=\prod_m(C\otimes_R Q_m(R))$, let $s$ be the transition shift, and define
$$H_R(C)^q=B_R(C)^q\oplus B_R(C)^{q-1},\qquad d(x,y)=(dx,(1-s)x-dy).$$
Let $\eta_C:C\to H_R(C)$ be $c\mapsto((c\otimes1)_m,0)$. Define $H_S(FC)$ and its unit by the same formulas. There is a natural chain isomorphism
$$h_C:F(H_R(C))\xrightarrow{\sim}H_S(FC),\qquad h_C F(\eta_C)=\eta_{FC},$$
using the canonical finite-biproduct comparisons and countable-product comparison, with the same ordering of Koszul factors. It descends to the ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated]. Thus invertibility of $\eta_C$ in the derived category implies invertibility of $\eta_{FC}$. The empty scalar list is allowed. This is a statement about the explicit signed model, not a choice of a map between unspecified cones.

proof.text:
Write $T_m(C)=C\otimes_R Q_m(R)$. For $J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,r\}$ let $e_J$ denote the tensor having degree $-1$ exactly in the factors indexed by $J$. The multiplication maps $M\otimes_R R\to M$, $z\otimes b\mapsto bz$, with inverse $z\mapsto z\otimes1$, commute with restrictions and thus give inverse sheaf maps by [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Expanding the finitely many summands in the total tensor of [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] gives $T_m(C)^q=\bigoplus_J C^{q+|J|}e_J$ up to these specified canonical identifications. Set $\epsilon(J,i)=(-1)^{|\{j\in J:j<i\}|}$. On the $J$ summand, for $z$ of degree $p=q+|J|$, the differential is
$$d(z e_J)=(d_Cz)e_J+\sum_{i\in J}(-1)^p\epsilon(J,i)a_i^m z e_{J\setminus\{i\}}.$$
The first sign is the total-tensor sign, and $\epsilon$ counts the earlier degree $-1$ factors. The transition $t_m:T_{m+1}(C)\to T_m(C)$ on the $J$ summand is multiplication by $a_J=\prod_{i\in J}a_i$. These are descriptions of module maps on finite summands; the notation does not assume an elementwise description of an arbitrary functor. For $r=0$ there is only $J=\varnothing$, and $a_J=1$.

proof.text: For any finite family $(M_J)$ define $b:F(\bigoplus_J M_J)\to\bigoplus_J F(M_J)$ by $\pi_Jb=F(\pi_J)$, and define $b^{-1}$ on the $J$th inclusion to be $F(\iota_J)$. Additivity [def-weil-pbc-additive-functor] gives $F(0)=0$ and preservation of finite sums of maps. Hence $F(\pi_J)F(\iota_K)=\delta_{JK}$ and $\sum_J F(\iota_J)F(\pi_J)=F(1)=1$, proving the two inverse identities. For a map $v$ between finite biproducts, its $(K,J)$ entry after conjugating $F(v)$ by these comparisons is $F(\pi_Kv\iota_J)$, by functoriality. Thus the comparisons are natural and carry every entry $a v$ to $aF(v)$ by the assumed $A$-linearity. The empty-family case is also valid: $1_{F(0)}=F(1_0)=F(0)=0$, so $F(0)$ is a zero object.

proof.text:
Apply the comparisons of Step 2 to the coordinates of Step 1, using precisely the same ordered subsets on the $R$ and $S$ sides. They give degreewise isomorphisms $\alpha_{m,C}:F(T_m(C))\to T_m(FC)$. Every entry of the differential in Step 1 is either $d_C$, zero, or a signed scalar $(-1)^{q+|J|}\epsilon(J,i)a_i^m$ times an identity. Its $F$-image is respectively $F(d_C)$, zero, or that same scalar times $1_{F(C^{q+|J|})}$. Thus $d\alpha_{m,C}=\alpha_{m,C}F(d)$ entry by entry, proving that $\alpha_{m,C}$ is a chain isomorphism. The transition entry $a_J1$ similarly gives
$$\alpha_{m,C}F(t_m^R)=t_m^S\alpha_{m+1,C}.$$
A chain map $u:C\to D$ acts on the $J$ summand by $u^{q+|J|}$, so the same entry calculation proves naturality in $C$. The inclusion $\iota_m:C\to T_m(C)$ into $J=\varnothing$ satisfies $\alpha_{m,C}F(\iota_m)=\iota_m'$ because Step 2 preserves the specified inclusions. This establishes tower and unit compatibility, without identifying $F(R)$ with $S$.

proof.text:
Let $\phi$ be the assumed invertible product comparison, degree by degree. Define $\beta_C:F(B_R(C))\to B_S(FC)$ by composing $\phi$ with the product of the $\alpha_{m,C}$ of Step 3. Its characterizing formula is
$$\operatorname{pr}_m\beta_C=\alpha_{m,C}F(\operatorname{pr}_m).$$
The product of the inverses $\alpha_{m,C}^{-1}$ is inverse to the product of the $\alpha_{m,C}$, as checked at each projection [def-weil-category-product], so $\beta_C$ is degreewise invertible. Projecting its differential equation to level $m$ reduces it to the chain equation for $\alpha_{m,C}$, hence it is a chain isomorphism. Projecting the shift equation gives
$$\operatorname{pr}_m\beta_CF(s_R)=\alpha_{m,C}F(t_m^R)F(\operatorname{pr}_{m+1})=t_m^S\operatorname{pr}_{m+1}\beta_C.$$
Consequently $\beta_CF(s_R)=s_S\beta_C$, and additivity gives $\beta_CF(1-s_R)=(1-s_S)\beta_C$. Naturality follows by projecting to each $m$ and using Step 3. All equalities concern the canonical product comparison, rather than an arbitrary product isomorphism.

proof.text:
Define $h_C^q$ as the canonical binary-biproduct comparison of Step 2 followed by $\beta_C^q\oplus\beta_C^{q-1}$. In these coordinates the source differential has block entries $F(d_B),0,F(1-s_R),-F(d_B)$. Step 4 and additivity [def-weil-pbc-additive-functor] identify them with the target entries $d_B,0,1-s_S,-d_B$. Equivalently, writing $(x,y)$ for the two source coordinates, both $d_Sh_C$ and $h_CF(d_R)$ have coordinates
$$(d_B\beta_Cx,\ (1-s_S)\beta_Cx-d_B\beta_Cy).$$
Thus $h_C$ is a chain map. Each $h_C^q$ is invertible by construction, and its degreewise inverse is a chain map by multiplying the differential equation by those inverses. The naturality of the binary comparison and of $\beta$ proves naturality of $h$. Directly, the stipulated fibre differential squares to zero because $d_B(1-s)=(1-s)d_B$, so its signs are consistent with the asserted model.

proof.text:
Let $e_C:C\to B_R(C)$ have projections $\iota_m$. Each $\iota_m$ is a chain map by the total differential [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], and $t_m\iota_{m+1}=\iota_m$ since transitions on the empty subset are identities. Hence $(1-s)e_C=0$, so $\eta_C=(e_C,0)$ is a chain map. Step 4, followed by the inclusion identity of Step 3, gives
$$\operatorname{pr}_m\beta_CF(e_C)=\alpha_{m,C}F(\iota_m)=\iota_m'=\operatorname{pr}_me_{FC}.$$
The product universal property [def-weil-category-product] proves $\beta_CF(e_C)=e_{FC}$. In the second fibre coordinate $F(0)=0$ [def-weil-pbc-additive-functor]. The canonical binary comparison therefore gives the strict chain-map equality $h_CF(\eta_C)=\eta_{FC}$, including its zero second coordinate.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sbc-koszul-fibre-linear-descent] separately to the sites $\mathcal C$ and $\mathcal D$, their commutative structure sheaves $R,S$, and the respective images of the scalar list in global sections. Its exact-countable-product hypothesis is assumed for each module category, and it permits $r=0$ and arbitrary unbounded coefficient complexes. Its displayed differential is exactly $(dx,(1-s)x-dy)$; its transitions, diagonal action on chain maps, and degree-zero coaugmentation are exactly those used here. It follows that $H_R,H_S$ preserve quasi-isomorphisms and induce functors on the ordinary unbounded derived categories with the same units. Independently [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated] applies to the assumed additive exact $F$ between the abelian module categories, and supplies its termwise derived functor $F_D$. Thus both composites $F_DH_R$ and $H_SF_D$ are defined on these derived categories; no boundedness or preservation of infinite coproducts by $F$ is needed.

proof.text: Use the localization universal property [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property](2) for the quasi-isomorphism localization from source complexes to $D(\operatorname{Mod}(R))$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Step 7 supplies the two factorizations; the localized chain isomorphisms of Step 5 form a natural isomorphism before this factorization, so they descend to $h:F_DH_R\xrightarrow{\sim}H_SF_D$. The same localization property (3), applied to Step 6, yields $h_CF_D(\eta_C)=\eta_{F_DC}$ under the canonical factorization identifications. If $\eta_C$ is invertible, its image under the functor $F_D$ is invertible, and $\eta_{F_DC}$ is their composite with the invertible $h_C$. Its inverse is $F_D(\eta_C^{-1})h_C^{-1}$. This proves the final implication for arbitrary derived objects as well as for displayed representatives.

proof.text: For the allowed empty list, $T_m(C)=C$ and all transitions are identities. Steps 3 and 4 reduce to identity finite-coordinate comparisons and the assumed comparison $F(\prod_m C)\cong\prod_m FC$. The first coordinate of $\eta_C$ is the diagonal into this product, so Step 6 remains valid. For $r=1$ the differential on the negative Koszul summand is exactly $(-1)^{q+1}a_1^m$ and the transition there is $a_1$, checking the two sign and transition formulas at the first nontrivial case. Scalars equal to zero or units cause no division in any step; no regular-sequence hypothesis has been used.
